newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish think-tank says industrial climate better.
newsitem.headline: Swedish think-tank says industrial climate better.

text.p: Sweden's National Economic Research Institute KI said on Wednesday the industrial climate in Sweden improved considerably in the second quarter of 1997.
"Industrial activity has improved considerably during the second quarter of this year," KI said in its Business Tendency Survey Manufacturing and Construction for June.
It said industry expected consumer prices to rise more in 1997 than they did three months ago.

"The expectations of manufacturing and mining in regard to general price growth (CPI) for the next 12 months was 1.5 percent in June. This is an upturn from March 1997 when the figure was one percent," KI said.
It said firms were optimistic about the third quarter.
"The inflow of orders is expected to continue to increase for both the domestic and the export markets. Growth in the export market is expected to remain strong," KI said.
"There are also plans for production increases in conjunction with estimated additional production capacity.
"Sales prices are expected to remain largely at unchanged levels, with the exception of the intermediate goods industry which is reporting continued increases," KI said.
It said production plans for the second half of the year were expansive. However, it said on the whole firms do not anticipate a need to increase employment in the third quarter.
"We know from experience, however, that firms usually underestimated actual growth during growth periods," it said.
KI, or Konjunkturinstitutet, also publishes monthly forecasts for the Swedish economy.
